newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Wheat Board retains soft wheat premium.
newsitem.headline: Australian Wheat Board retains soft wheat premium.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Thursday strengthening U.S. markets had helped it to again guarantee soft wheat growers a $5 a tonne premium to the Australian Standard White (ASW) 10 percent protein pool.
"This is a great result for soft growers given the recent world market volatility," said AWB soft wheat product team leader Todd Buck in a statement.
Buck said the AWB had offered the A$5 premium for the third year in succession.
He said the AWB's niche marketing strategies, aimed mainly out of its Hong Kong office at southern China, had also helped demand for the product.
"The market has grown from zero to 100,000 tonnes over the past five years and is likely to surpass South Korea as our biggest buyer of soft wheat in 1997," Buck said.
"Our ability to produce low protein wheat is very important to this market and is gaining a good reputation as a steamed bread wheat," he said.
Buck added the soft wheat export market was growing faster than production increases and it seemed likely demand would reach 500,000 tonnes by 2000.

"The AWB is always looking at new segregations, new varieties and new areas for soft wheat but it is important we work closely with the grower associations to make sure they are successful," AWB senior wheat merchant Lisa Wilson said.
